transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because my answers get all over the place. Someone at work will ask when a ring repair will be ready, and I’ll start talking about invoices, then garden soil, then the mortgage papers. I can see them getting confused, and I know I’ve lost them.
Lately, have you found yourself needing much less sleep than usual while still feeling full of energy?
I’m not really full of energy. I lie awake going over receipts and odd thoughts until two or three, then I’m up again before dawn and can’t settle back down.
You mentioned having odd thoughts while lying awake—could you share an example of what those thoughts are about?

I know it sounds odd, but I’ve started feeling like some customers come in to see if I’m missing payments. They ask a lot about the new showroom, and even though my husband says they’re just being friendly, it feels like they’re checking up on me.
Over the past few weeks, have you been feeling down, depressed, or hopeless?
Yeah. Most mornings I wake up with this flat, heavy sadness. It’s like all the color has drained out of the house before I even get to the shop.
Have you experienced these suspicious thoughts or scattered thinking during times when your mood was normal and you weren't feeling depressed?

Before the depression really set in, I was still running my classes and gardening, but for a few weeks I kept hearing noises from the polishing room and worrying that customers were watching the business.
Looking at the entire time you have been dealing with these suspicious thoughts and noises, have you felt depressed for most of that time?
Yes. For most of the time, I’ve felt bleak and guilty, and my sleep and appetite have been poor. It hasn’t just been a couple of bad weeks—it’s been there day after day.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets criteria for Schizoaffective disorder, depressive type (F25.1). She presents with concurrent major depressive symptoms (depressed mood, insomnia, poor appetite, feelings of guilt and bleakness) and active-phase psychotic symptoms (disorganized thinking/derailment, persecutory delusions, auditory hallucinations). Crucially, she confirms experiencing psychotic symptoms (hallucinatory noises and persecutory beliefs) for several weeks in the absence of prominent mood symptoms, and depressive symptoms have been present for the majority of the total illness duration.
